papers.title: GamSleepNet: A Lightweight Automatic Sleep Staging Framework Based on Gabor Feature Extraction and Mamba Sequence Modeling for Single-Channel EEG.
papers.summary: Proposed GamSleepNet, a lightweight single-channel EEG sleep-staging framework combining improved Gabor feature extraction with a learnable filter branch and a Mamba selective state-space model, plus teacher-student feature alignment and two-stage training. On Sleep-EDF it reached 87.86% accuracy and 82.62% macro-F1 with only 30.86k parameters, improving recognition of difficult N1 and REM stages and remaining stable under low SNR and label scarcity.

papers.title: A Temporally Causal Two-Layer Framework for Wearable EEG Sleep Staging and Short-Horizon Sleep-Transition Forecasting.
papers.summary: Developed a temporally causal two-layer framework for wearable EEG in which a five-stage sleep classifier (M0) fed cross-fitted stage-probability histories to a second layer (M1) forecasting transitions from wake/N1 to N2/N3/REM within 60-120 s. M0 achieved 0.830 accuracy and 0.704 macro-F1, and M1 reached AUROC 0.801, 0.791, and 0.786 at 60, 90, and 120 s respectively, with cross-device limitations identified on Muse S Gen2 recordings.

papers.title: MG-STNet: A Compact Multi-Granularity Spatiotemporal Network for Adaptive Sleep Staging.
papers.summary: Proposed MG-STNet, a compact multi-granularity spatiotemporal network for sleep staging using parallel downsampling branches, global-local feature recalibration, adaptive spatiotemporal convolution, and temporal attention encoding. On Sleep-EDF-20 and Sleep-EDF-78 it achieved 87.3% and 84.5% accuracy (four-channel, 46.6K parameters) and 86.6% and 83.2% (single-channel), offering a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off.

papers.title: Operational Definitions of Transition Onset Shape EEG Biomarker Timing in Drowsiness: A Single-Channel Method Comparison.
papers.summary: Built a benchmarking framework to test how operational definitions of transition onset affect EEG drowsiness lead-time claims, applying seven onset estimators and 32 single-channel frontal EEG features across 17 participants with replication in DROZY. Estimator choice shifted onsets by minutes and detection coverage ranged from 45% to 100%, while no estimator showed excess pre-anchor onsets versus surrogate data, prompting proposed interpretability criteria, evidence levels, and a reporting checklist.

papers.title: Neural State Geometry: Unifying Amplitude Landscapes, Coherency Geometry and Information Geometry for EEG State Estimation.
papers.summary: Introduced Neural State Geometry (NSG), a sensor-space EEG framework integrating a Neural Amplitude Landscape mapped to thermodynamic quantities, Stokes/coherency geometry, and quantum-information-inspired state-space geometry, evaluated via synthetic tests, amplitude-model comparison, a cognitive fatigue example, and a transcranial focused ultrasound feasibility case. NSG descriptors showed selectivity in synthetic tests, improved held-out prediction over several amplitude models but not lognormal, and revealed state deformation associated with fatigue and TUS application.

papers.title: Sparse EEG neurodynamics of hypoglycemia in type 1 diabetes with personal euglycemic baseline adaptation.
papers.summary: Benchmarked 24 EEG models under leave-one-subject-out validation for hypoglycemia detection in type 1 diabetes and applied Personal Euglycemic Baseline Adaptation (PEBA); PEBA raised balanced accuracy (e.g., 0.68 to 0.83 for feature-domain Sinc-SSNET) while channel/feature sparsification cut parameters by 88.51%-99.88% with the F7 log-theta descriptor increasing during hypoglycemia in 88.2% of participants.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Features for Distinguishing VS/UWS from MCS: A Comprehensive Univariate Evaluation with Exploratory Multivariate Analysis.
papers.summary: Compared ten resting-state EEG feature families across 53 VS/UWS, 55 MCS, and 48 healthy controls, finding microstate transition probabilities the strongest univariate discriminator (D-to-A AUC 0.708) while a Sparse Group Lasso model in nested cross-validation reached only mean AUC 0.632, with microstate dynamics and nonlinear complexity most consistently selected.

papers.title: Participant-Specific Adaptive Label Smoothing Using Subjective Workload Responses for Cognitive Workload Classification from EEG.
papers.summary: Proposed participant-specific adaptive label smoothing, where changes in subjective workload between rest and task set target confidence, and evaluated it on the STEW EEG dataset with a feature-based CNN and a multi-scale Swin Transformer under participant-disjoint cross-validation, achieving the highest macro F1 (0.768 and 0.796) and ROC AUC (0.844 and 0.878) under stratified normalization.

papers.title: Incremental Value of EEG Beyond EMG for Participant-Independent Forecasting of Bilateral Lower-Limb Joint Angles.
papers.summary: Tested whether EEG adds predictive value beyond EMG for forecasting six bilateral lower-limb joint angles ~124.6 ms ahead across 163 treadmill trials from 57 participants using participant-disjoint nested validation, and found no significant gain from multimodal fusion, with shared-penalty fusion reducing R2 for left knee and left ankle.

papers.title: Auditable Multiscale EEG Fusion for Offline Cognitive Workload Decoding in COG-BCI.
papers.summary: Evaluated an auditable multiscale spectral/covariance EEG decoder for 0-back versus 2-back cognitive workload in the COG-BCI dataset using nominal-unit-held-out validation, reporting mean window balanced accuracy of 80.70% and mean unit AUC of 0.8770, with no reliable advantage for single temporal widths and a 16.39-point BA drop without target alignment.

papers.title: AI-Driven Non-Invasive Scalp EEG Biosensing for Real-Time Seizure Prediction Using Lightweight Gradient Boosting Ensembles.
papers.summary: Developed a computationally lightweight, patient-independent machine learning pipeline using an ensemble of regularized XGBoost and LightGBM on CHB-MIT scalp EEG, and on four completely unseen subjects achieved 100% event-level seizure sensitivity (34/34) with a false alarm rate of 0.415/h and a mean prediction horizon of 17.03 min at 0.0057 ms per window.

papers.title: When Subject-Level Validation Is Not Enough: Acquisition Format Confounding in a Public Depression Electroencephalography Archive.
papers.summary: Audited the public Mumtaz/HUSM depression EEG archive and found that, despite 0.9158 balanced accuracy under nested participant-disjoint validation, acquisition metadata were label-aligned: 22/26 controls had 22-channel EDF files versus only 1/27 depression-labeled participants (Fisher's exact p=6.80×10-10), so participant isolation alone does not establish depression-specific EEG information.

papers.title: Objective-to-Subjective Sleep Discrepancy in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Pilot EEG Study.
papers.summary: In a pilot study of 22 hospitalized rheumatoid arthritis patients using portable single-channel EEG, subjective total sleep time exceeded EEG-derived TST by a median of 82.75 min and was uncorrelated with it, with a more positive discrepancy associated with lower albumin, higher CRP, glucocorticoid use, higher DAS28-CRP, and functional disability.

papers.title: Source-reconstructed EEG graph signal processing: Pitfalls and workarounds.
papers.summary: Investigated methodological biases in source-reconstructed EEG graph signal processing, showing that uncorrected SVD polarity ambiguity inflates high-frequency graph power (mitigated by a proposed sign-control method) and that electrical source imaging spatial leakage inflates low-frequency content, with stronger effects during spikes and for eLORETA and Euclidean-distance connectomes.

papers.title: TurboRhythmPat and Directed Rhythm Lobish: An Explainable Multi-Selector EEG Model for Recognising Attack and Post-Attack States in Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.summary: Introduces TurboRhythmPat, an explainable EEG model coding 15 s segments into 1805 source-rhythm-target routes with multi-selector feature selection and self-organised tkNN fusion, plus Directed Rhythm Lobish for decoding decisions. In 19 MS patients and 19 controls under nested leave-one-subject-out validation, attack vs. post-attack states were separated at 65.61% segment-level and 76.32% recording-level accuracy, with patient-level accuracy above chance in 13/19 patients.

papers.title: Frequency-embedded sequence learning for multi-class EEG-to-text interface.
papers.summary: Proposed a lightweight 1D-CNN pipeline for 5-class EEG-to-text decoding trained on time-domain EEG versus frequency-embedded PSD sequences, reaching mean intra-subject accuracies of 46.1% and 64.4% respectively (peaks 54% and 82%), while inter-subject pooled performance remained near chance (~23-25%).

papers.title: A whole-brain neural mass model incorporating astrocyte calcium dynamics for simulating tDCS-induced EEG modulation.
papers.summary: Proposes a whole-brain neural mass model incorporating astrocyte calcium dynamics alongside pyramidal and interneuron populations, interconnected via the human connectome across 76 cortical areas, to simulate tDCS-induced EEG modulation with realistic head meshes and electric-field distribution. Simulations showed increased alpha-band power and greater high-frequency power attributable to astrocyte-mediated tDCS effects.

papers.title: Machine Learning Decoding of Dystonic States from EEG-LFP Signals in GPi-DBS: A Multimodal Case Study.
papers.summary: In a single pediatric patient with generalized dystonia undergoing GPi-DBS, synchronized EEG, LFP, and EMG recordings across seven sessions were used to train regularized logistic regression classifiers for decoding dystonic muscle activity from quantitative EMG labels. The combined EEG-LFP model achieved balanced accuracy 0.74 in mixed leave-one-recording-out validation (sensitivity 0.78, specificity 0.70), with moderately degraded performance (0.66-0.70) on unseen stimulation intensities.

papers.title: Source-Level Multiscale Granger Causality from Preictal Scalp EEG Identifies Candidate Seizure-Onset Zones in Drug-Resistant Focal Epilepsy.
papers.summary: Combined sLORETA source reconstruction with multiscale spectral Granger causality on preictal scalp EEG in 14 drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients to identify candidate seizure-onset zones via regional net causal flow in the beta band. Candidate SOZ regions were concordant with clinical localization in 6/7 resected participants and 3/5 scorable prospective participants (9/12 overall), with top-ranked regions showing net causal inflow.

papers.title: EEG Theta Power as an Indicator of Cognitive Workload in Student Pilots.
papers.summary: Measured scalp EEG theta (4-8 Hz) power at eight locations in ten student pilots during baseline and three high-fidelity PC-21 flight simulator modules of differing difficulty, with NASA-TLX workload ratings after each phase. Theta power was higher in the most cognitively demanding phase across frontal, temporal, and occipital regions, but correlations between theta measures and subjective workload ratings were weak and inconsistent at the group level.

papers.title: MSST-TCN: A Spatially Adaptive Multi-Scale Temporal Convolutional Network for Resting-State EEG-Based Depression Recognition.
papers.summary: Proposes MSST-TCN, a model combining spatial adaptive filtering, multi-scale dilated convolution, and temporal attention pooling for resting-state EEG depression recognition. On 53 MODMA participants under stratified five-fold cross-validation, it achieved 84.71 ± 2.49% mean window-level accuracy and 81.13% participant-level accuracy, 6.41 percentage points above a single-scale TCN baseline.

papers.title: Age-Adjusted Exploratory Analysis of Spectral, Aperiodic, and Microstate Electroencephalography Features in Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.summary: Examined age-adjusted associations between resting-state EEG spectral, aperiodic, and microstate features and multiple sclerosis in the BrainLat dataset (32 MS, 32 controls). After FDR correction, global bandwidth, global aperiodic offset, and channel-wise aperiodic offset were significantly associated with diagnosis, whereas central frequency, exponent, power spectral density, and all microstate measures were not; the non-overlapping age ranges limit interpretation.

papers.title: Physiology-Guided Spiking Neural Networks for EEG Motor-Imagery Recognition.
papers.summary: Introduces PG-SNN, a spiking neural network that embeds sensorimotor physiological priors into event coding, electrode-prior graph spatial propagation, and multi-timescale spike dynamics for motor-imagery EEG decoding. It reached 84.72% accuracy (kappa 0.796) on BCI Competition IV-2a and 71.28% (kappa 0.617) on EEGMMIDB, exceeding matched ANN and SNN baselines.

papers.title: Exploratory Assessment of Portable EEG- and PPG-Derived Indices Following High-Intensity Exercise Under Partial Sleep Restriction in Young Men.
papers.summary: Exploratory randomized study comparing 20 normal-sleep and 20 sleep-restricted young men on portable prefrontal EEG and PPG indices, heart rate recovery, and perceived exertion after the Harvard Step Test. Sleep restriction showed a significant group × time interaction for theta-to-beta ratio (increase only in the restricted group), altered HRV/sympathetic/parasympathetic indices, lower early heart rate recovery, and higher perceived exertion.

papers.title: EEG Functional Connectivity for Consumer Preference Prediction: Statistical Network Analysis and Stable Connectivity Signatures.
papers.summary: Evaluated EEG functional connectivity (Phase Locking Value and Normalized Mutual Information) for predicting consumer preference using the NeuMa dataset with LASSO feature selection and multiple classifiers. Preferred-product viewing was associated with widespread connectivity reductions, especially NMI in the delta band; PLV with Naive Bayes achieved the highest balanced accuracy of 0.699, while NMI-derived features dominated feature-selection stability.

papers.title: Development and Evaluation of a Cap-Mounted Tripolar Concentric Ring Electrode System with a Central Gel-Delivery Opening for tEEG and EEG Recording.
papers.summary: Developed a gold-plated copper tripolar concentric ring electrode with a 2 mm central gel-delivery opening and 3D-printed cap-mounted holder, and evaluated it in ten healthy adults at occipital hair-bearing sites. The system recorded identifiable VEPs (peaks near 105 and 141 ms), eEEG VEPs at O1/O2 strongly correlated with Pz (median r=0.897 and 0.938), and alpha power increased significantly with eye closure in gel-coupled tEEG channels (Holm-adjusted p=0.0195).

papers.title: Decision-Aligned Value Learning for Selective Adoption of EEG Fusion in Human-Robot Collaboration
papers.summary: Proposed VECTA, a selective EEG fusion framework that treats whether to adopt an EEG-informed prediction as a sample-wise incremental-value estimation problem, separating Fusion prediction generation from Base-vs-Fusion adoption decisions. Across three HRC datasets, matched Fusion outperformed shuffled controls, estimated gains tracked realized gains (Spearman 0.347-0.612; positive-gain AUROCs 0.708-0.842), and VECTA achieved the highest mean normalized AUBC under budget constraints among evaluated selective-decision methods.

papers.title: Quantitative EEG Differences Across Two Sedation Conditions in a Child with Epilepsy: A Case Report.
papers.summary: A within-subject case report compared quantitative interictal EEG in a child with congenital CMV-associated structural epilepsy under propofol versus chloral hydrate sedation using duration-matched 15.52-min segments. The chloral hydrate recording showed higher spike frequency (14.11 vs. 4.12 spikes/min; rate ratio 3.42) and spike index (84.95% vs. 27.96%), with lower SEF95 and greater delta predominance under propofol, though recordings occurred about a year apart and differences cannot be attributed specifically to the sedatives.

papers.title: PHQ-9-Guided Ordinal Contrastive Learning for Severity-Aware EEG Depression Representation Learning.
papers.summary: Proposed PHQ-9-guided ordinal contrastive learning (CE+OC), using PHQ-9 severity distances as privileged ordinal supervision during training while requiring only EEG at inference, evaluated on MODMA with leave-one-subject-out cross-validation in 53 subjects. CE+OC increased cross-validated held-out PHQ-9 rank correlation from 7.8% to 33.6% (p=0.031) and reduced mean absolute PHQ-9 error from 27.8% to 22.8% of the scale range, with descriptive diagnostic differences including AUC rising from 59.8% to 69.3%.

papers.title: Multidimensional Electrophysiological Responses to TMS on the Primary Motor Cortex: A TMS-EEG Characterization of Immediate Cortical Responses.
papers.summary: A randomized within-subject crossover TMS-EEG study in 17 healthy adults characterized immediate multidimensional cortical responses to 10 Hz rTMS, 1 Hz rTMS, and iTBS over the left primary motor cortex. Protocol-specific profiles emerged: 10 Hz increased P30 (0.17 to 0.89 μV) and broad 15.5-45 Hz PSD, 1 Hz reduced P30 (0.68 to 0.39 μV) and PSD, and iTBS reduced N45 magnitude and P60.

papers.title: Is Swimming Training Experience Associated with Better Sensorimotor Control in Water? An Exploratory Study of Upper-Limb Joint Position Sense, EEG Activity, and Subjective Workload.
papers.summary: Compared shoulder and elbow joint position sense, resting and task-related alpha/beta EEG power, and NASA-TLX workload across swimmers, Wushu athletes, and untrained participants on land and in water. Swimming experience was associated with greater water-land increases in resting-state alpha power and lower physical demand in water, but not with better joint-position accuracy or distinct task-related cortical modulation.

papers.title: EEG Emotion Recognition Based on Azimuthal Equidistant Projection and a Multiscale Residual Temporal Network.
papers.summary: Proposed an EEG emotion recognition framework combining azimuthal equidistant projection for topologically preserved differential-entropy feature maps with a multiscale residual temporal network (MRTNet). Reported average accuracies of 95.1% for four-class classification on DEAP and 93.1% for three-class classification on SEED, with Grad-CAM responses localized to frontal and temporal regions.

papers.title: Neural dynamics of resting-state EEG microstates in youth major depressive disorder with suicidal ideation.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional resting-state EEG microstate analysis in 95 drug-naive youth with major depressive disorder (53 with suicidal ideation, 42 without) versus 82 healthy controls. Suicidal ideation was associated with higher occurrence, coverage, and duration of microstate A, reduced microstate B indices, reduced microstate D occurrence, and altered transition probabilities, with BSI-C scores correlating with C-to-B transition probability.

papers.title: Hybrid EEG-EOG Brain-Computer Interface for Virtual-Reality Powered Mobility Training in Children with Severe Neuromotor Disabilities: A Multiple-Case Feasibility Study.
papers.summary: Multiple-case feasibility study of a hybrid EEG-EOG brain-computer interface integrated with a virtual reality powered wheelchair simulator in six children and adolescents with severe neuromotor disabilities, using kinesthetic motor imagery for steering and EOG blinks for discrete commands. Mean online classification accuracy was 67% (77% in successful evaluations), four participants completed the protocol, and workload and VR tolerability were acceptable.

papers.title: From hemodynamics to function: the role of fNIRS and hybrid EEG-fNIRS systems in next-generation assistive technologies for rehabilitation.
papers.summary: Systematically reviewed the evolution of assistive technology control modalities and the technical capabilities and limitations of fNIRS and hybrid EEG-fNIRS systems for rehabilitation and brain-computer interfaces. Concludes that hybrid EEG-fNIRS combines high temporal with spatial/hemodynamic information to improve accuracy and adaptability toward more user-centered rehabilitation technologies.

papers.title: Differential Neurophysiological Signatures of Asymptomatic Carotid and Intracranial Atherosclerotic Stenosis: A Multimodal Resting-State EEG Study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional multimodal resting-state EEG study of 68 participants, asymptomatic carotid stenosis and asymptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis showed shared reductions in microstate A coverage and A-to-C transitions, but ACS additionally had shortened MsA duration, reduced alpha power, and increased alpha-band connectivity within a distributed NBS network, whereas aICAS showed increased B–D microstate transitions without a significant NBS component. Selected microstate measures remained associated with Trail Making Test performance and yielded moderate cross-validated ROC discrimination (AUC 0.675–0.744).

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Auditory Electrophysiological Biomarkers in Alzheimer's Disease and Hearing Loss: A Critical Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This critical narrative review synthesizes evidence linking hearing loss, Alzheimer's disease, and auditory electrophysiology, and evaluates machine learning, deep learning, self-supervised learning, explainable AI, and multimodal modeling for extracting auditory electrophysiological biomarkers such as EEG, ERP, AECP, ABR, cochlear microphonics, and DPOAE measures. It also identifies methodological limitations including small samples, heterogeneous acquisition, limited external validation and interpretability, and data leakage risks, and proposes directions for trustworthy multimodal AI biomarker systems.

papers.title: Long-Term Music Training Is Associated with Auditory-Frontal Cortical Responses in Mandarin-Speaking Children with Cochlear Implants: A Clinical High-Density EEG Study.
papers.summary: In a clinical high-density EEG study of 30 Mandarin-speaking children with cochlear implants grouped by cumulative music-training duration, behavioral aided hearing thresholds and speech-perception accuracy were comparable across groups, but source-localized mismatch negativity showed progressively stronger prefrontal activation with longer training, most evident for vowel and consonant deviants. Adjusted linear models linked longer training duration to prefrontal activation for intensity (p=0.002) and tone (p=0.022) deviants, with marginal associations for consonant and vowel deviants.

papers.title: Detecting cognitive motor dissociation in unresponsive brain-injured patients: a prospective cohort study using active task-based EEG.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 56 clinically unresponsive brain-injured patients, active task-based EEG during motor imagery detected cognitive motor dissociation in 6 patients (10.7%); CMD-positive patients descriptively had more favorable 6-month outcomes (2/6 vs 4/50) and no deaths versus 16% mortality in CMD-negative patients, though differences were not statistically significant. Nine of ten healthy controls were task-positive, and most volunteers reported drowsiness, prompting the authors to call for more sensitive, patient-adapted paradigms.

papers.title: Changes in Clinical Management Related to Continuous Versus Routine Electroencephalogram in Critically Ill Adults: Analysis of a Randomized Trial.
papers.summary: This ancillary analysis of the randomized CERTA trial compared continuous versus repeated routine EEG in 364 critically ill adults with altered consciousness and found more clinical management changes with cEEG (58.2% vs 45.6%, p=0.018), driven mainly by anti-seizure medication modification (22.0% vs 12.1%, p=0.012). After adjusting for ASM modifications, 6-month mortality and functional outcome remained similar between EEG groups, indicating that increased management changes did not translate into improved outcomes.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
